settings.title: Settings
settings.languageHint: Changes apply immediately, no restart needed.
settings.densityHint: Compact shows more tracks on screen.

settings.qualityHint: How to pick the file to keep among duplicates, and when a bitrate counts as low.

errors.offlineFile: File not found or drive disconnected.

errors.artwork: This image could not be used.

writeErrors.exists: a file with the same name is already there; nothing was overwritten.

writeErrors.convert_not_wav: it is not a WAV file.
writeErrors.convert_unsupported: this WAV cannot be converted losslessly (floating point or unusual format).
writeErrors.convert_exists: an AIFF with the same name already exists.

move.hint: The files change folder on the drive. Nothing is overwritten: a file with the same name already there is reported and skipped.
move.problems_one: {{count}} track will not be moved (see the list).
move.problems_other: {{count}} tracks will not be moved (see the list).

onboarding.welcomeText: A few settings before you start. Everything can be changed later in Settings.
onboarding.foldersText: Choose the folder where your music lives. If it is on an external drive, plug it in now.
onboarding.inboxHint: For example your Beatport or Bandcamp downloads folder. New files there will be identified and tagged automatically.
onboarding.exfat: Tip: for a drive used on both Windows and Mac, the exFAT format is the most convenient.
onboarding.onlineText: From phase 2, the application will be able to complete your tags and artwork from MusicBrainz, Deezer and iTunes. A free AcoustID key (optional) will recognise badly named tracks. Nothing is sent without your consent.
onboarding.tip1: Organise and rename your tracks here before importing them into Rekordbox: they will never have broken links there.
onboarding.tip2: After changing tags, use “Reload Tag” in Rekordbox so it reads the files again.
onboarding.tip3: For WAV files, Rekordbox reads title, artist, album and genre, but not the artwork.

online.queued_other: {{count}} tracks added to the online search

online.queuedOffline_other: Offline: the search for {{count}} tracks will run when the network is back

crop.hint: Drag the square to choose the part to keep; pull the bottom-right corner to make it bigger or smaller.

inbox.noFolderText: Choose the folder where your new tracks arrive (Beatport, Bandcamp downloads…). Each new file will be identified, tagged, given artwork and renamed automatically when it is safe.
inbox.rekordboxTip: A track processed here before importing it into Rekordbox will never have a broken link there.

onlineSettings.step2: Create your user key (required from 1 January 2027) at

onlineSettings.keyError: The system keychain refused to save the key.
onlineSettings.contactHint: MusicBrainz asks for a way to contact the application (website address or e-mail). Nothing is sent while this field is empty.

result.invalid_user_key: user key rejected: check it on acoustid.org/api-key

duplicates.intro: Exact copies, and the same track in another format or quality (sound compared on this computer, no internet). Two different versions (Original Mix, Extended Mix, Radio Edit, remix) are never grouped.
duplicates.searching: Looking for duplicates. You can keep working.
duplicates.alreadySearching: A duplicate search is already running.
duplicates.none: No duplicates found. Run a search after adding tracks.
duplicates.suspect: Suspicious quality: treble cut at {{khz}} kHz.
duplicates.previewHint: The kept file receives what it is missing, then the others go to quarantine (nothing is deleted, everything can be undone).
duplicates.transfer: Carry rating, tags and cover over to the kept file

quarantine.intro: Discarded files are kept in a “_Quarantaine” folder on the same disk, with their original folder structure. They take no extra space and go back to their place in one click.
quarantine.gone: File missing from the quarantine folder
quarantine.confirmText_one: {{count}} file ({{size}}) will be moved to the system trash.
quarantine.confirmText_other: {{count}} files ({{size}}) will be moved to the system trash.
quarantine.confirmHint: You can still recover them from the trash, but no longer from the app.
quarantine.confirmOffline_one: {{count}} file on a disconnected disk will be left aside.
quarantine.confirmOffline_other: {{count}} files on disconnected disks will be left aside.

quality.title: Quality check
quality.spectrogramHint: Time runs left to right, treble is at the top. A sharp horizontal limit with only black above it gives away a file made from an MP3 or AAC.
quality.cutoff: Sharp treble cut detected at {{khz}} kHz.

detail.fakeLossless: sharp cut at {{khz}} kHz: probably a converted MP3 or AAC (fake lossless)
detail.upscaled: cut at {{khz}} kHz for {{kbps}} kbit/s claimed: probably upscaled
detail.truncated: truncated file: {{got}} s readable out of {{expected}} s

health.analyzing: Quality check running in the background. Counters update as it goes.
health.alreadyAnalyzing: The quality check is already running.
health.analyzeHint: The quality check reads each file in full (damaged audio, truncated file, fake lossless). It changes nothing. Allow a few seconds per track on a USB disk.
health.allGood: Nothing to report: your library is in good health.
health.onlineQueued_one: {{count}} track added to the online search. Uncertain cases will go to “To review”.
health.onlineQueued_other: {{count}} tracks added to the online search. Uncertain cases will go to “To review”.
health.syncHint: Rekordbox only reads the RIFF INFO part of WAV files. It will be rewritten to match the full tags (ID3). The audio is not touched.
health.relocatePick: Folder to search for missing files
health.relocateNone: None of the missing files were found in this folder.
health.relocateHint: The track records (locks, history, online results) will be linked to these files. No file is moved.

playlists.intro: A playlist holds the tracks you add to it. A smart filter fills itself from its rules (genre, rating, BPM…). Both export to M3U and to Rekordbox.
playlists.noneStatic: No playlists. Select tracks, then “… › Add to a playlist”.
playlists.deleteText: Only the playlist is deleted: tracks and files are not touched.
playlists.name: Name
playlists.invalidRules: A rule is incomplete or invalid.

rekordbox.intro: The app never touches the Rekordbox database: it uses the official XML file. Import your collection to know which tracks are in Rekordbox (“RB” badge) and protect them.
rekordbox.imported: {{matched}} of {{total}} tracks found in your library.
rekordbox.stale: Your Rekordbox export is more than 7 days old. Re-import it to keep the badges accurate.
rekordbox.staleToast: Your Rekordbox export is more than 7 days old.
rekordbox.howExport: How do I export the XML from Rekordbox?
rekordbox.howExport3: Save the file, then import it here.
rekordbox.protectedHint: A track that is in Rekordbox is never renamed or moved automatically, and a manual rename or move shows a warning first. Its tags can still be edited.
rekordbox.renameAlert_one: {{count}} track is in Rekordbox: it will show as missing there after this change. The path log (Settings › Rekordbox) will help you relocate it.
rekordbox.renameAlert_other: {{count}} tracks are in Rekordbox: they will show as missing there after this change. The path log (Settings › Rekordbox) will help you relocate them.
rekordbox.quarantineAlert_one: {{count}} discarded file is in Rekordbox ({{names}}): it will show as missing there.
rekordbox.quarantineAlert_other: {{count}} discarded files are in Rekordbox ({{names}}): they will show as missing there.
rekordbox.quarantineAlertSelection_one: {{count}} of the chosen tracks is in Rekordbox: it will show as missing there once in quarantine.
rekordbox.quarantineAlertSelection_other: {{count}} of the chosen tracks are in Rekordbox: they will show as missing there once in quarantine.
rekordbox.badgeReload: In Rekordbox · tags changed, to reload
rekordbox.reloadHint: Rekordbox only sees tag changes after “Reload Tag”. Export this list as M3U8, import it into Rekordbox, select all its tracks, then right-click › “Reload Tag”. Then clear the list.
rekordbox.journalHint: Every rename or move is logged (old path; new path). This CSV file helps relocate files in Rekordbox.
rekordbox.journalOnly: Only tracks that are in Rekordbox
rekordbox.exportXmlIntro: Creates an XML file with your ratings, tags and playlists. In Rekordbox: Preferences › Advanced › Database › “rekordbox xml”, choose this file, then open the “rekordbox xml” section of the left panel.
rekordbox.exportXmlHint: The file holds each track's location, title, artists, album, genre, year, key, remixer, label, version and rating, plus the ticked playlists (smart filters are exported with their current tracks).
rekordbox.scopePlaylists: Only the tracks of the ticked playlists
rekordbox.backupHint: Tip: back up your Rekordbox library (File › Library › Backup Library) before importing anything.
rekordbox.skippedOffline_one: {{count}} track on a disconnected disk was left out.
rekordbox.skippedOffline_other: {{count}} tracks on disconnected disks were left out.
rekordbox.wavNote: Rekordbox only reads 5 fields in a WAV (title, artist, album, genre, comment) and no cover. To see all the information and the cover, you can convert WAV files to AIFF (library “…” menu): the audio stays bit-identical.

update.title: Updates
update.hint: At startup, the app asks GitHub for the latest version number. Nothing else is sent.

convert.hint: The audio stays bit-identical: only the container changes. The AIFF gets all the tags and the cover, which Rekordbox can read. Each file is checked before it is kept.
convert.rekordboxAlert_one: {{count}} of these WAV files is already in Rekordbox: the AIFF will be a new track there (Rekordbox ratings, cues and playlists do not follow).
convert.rekordboxAlert_other: {{count}} of these WAV files are already in Rekordbox: the AIFF files will be new tracks there (Rekordbox ratings, cues and playlists do not follow).
convert.after: The original WAV files go to quarantine: you can restore them, or empty the quarantine once the AIFF files are checked. Ctrl+Z undoes everything.

titleFormat.label: Title written in files
titleFormat.hint: DJ players (and Rekordbox) often show only the title in playlists. Choose what it contains. In the application, title, version and artist stay separate.

options.title: Title only: “Strobe”
options.artistTitleVersion: Main artist, title and version: “Deadmau5 - Strobe (Extended Mix)”

titleFormat.confirmText_one: The title field of {{formatted}} track will be rewritten with the chosen format.
titleFormat.confirmText_other: The title field of {{formatted}} tracks will be rewritten with the chosen format.
titleFormat.confirmHint: Only the title field changes; the audio is not touched. Files already written this way are left as they are. Ctrl+Z restores the previous titles. In Rekordbox, then run “Reload Tag” (“To reload” list).
titleFormat.doneWithFailures_one: Titles rewritten, except {{count}} file (disk unplugged or unreadable file).
titleFormat.doneWithFailures_other: Titles rewritten, except {{count}} files (disks unplugged or unreadable files).

watch.noSource: No source is enabled. Enable one in settings: only the country, genre or label you look for is sent.
watch.chartsDisabled: Charts use Apple Music or Deezer, currently disabled.
watch.releasesDisabled: New releases use MusicBrainz, currently disabled.
watch.deezerCountryHint: Deezer picks the country of its charts from your internet connection.
watch.musicbrainzHint: MusicBrainz is a free database run by volunteers: very complete for big labels, sometimes behind for small electronic labels.
watch.inLibraryHint: A track by the same artist with the same title is already in your library.
watch.wishIntro: Titles you spotted. When a file by the same artist with the same title arrives in your library (Inbox or indexing), it switches to “Found” automatically. The application downloads nothing: links open the stores in your browser.
watch.wishEmpty: Your wishlist is empty. Add titles from charts or new releases.
watch.spotifyLinkHint: A linked Spotify account lets you add these titles to one of its playlists.

errors.offline: No internet connection. The wishlist remains usable.
errors.network: The service did not answer correctly. Try again later.
errors.invalid_setting: This source is disabled or a setting is missing (Settings › Releases).
errors.not_linked: The Spotify account is no longer linked (expired or revoked). Reconnect it in Settings › Releases.
errors.keyring: The system keychain is not accessible: the account cannot be linked.

spotify.title: Add to a Spotify playlist
spotify.summary: {{found}} of {{total}} title(s) found. Check the matches and untick the wrong ones.
spotify.checkHint: Search uses the ISRC code when known, otherwise artist and title (including the version when possible).
spotify.unlinked: Spotify account unlinked. The token was erased.

settings.title: Releases
settings.hint: The Releases screen looks up charts and new releases. Each source stays disabled until you enable it. Only the country, genre or label you look for is sent, never anything about you or your library.
settings.apple: charts by country (most played songs and albums, updated daily).
settings.deezer: charts by genre (country inferred by Deezer from your connection).
settings.musicbrainz: new releases of a label or a country (free database).
settings.spotifyHint: Linking your account lets you add wishlist titles to a Spotify playlist. Spotify requires you to create a free “app” in your name (Premium subscription required by Spotify). No password is typed into DJ Library Manager: you sign in in your browser, and the token is stored in the system keychain.
settings.step1: Sign in to the Spotify developer site and create an app (“Create app”, tick “Web API”):
settings.step3: Save, then copy the app's “Client ID” and paste it below.
settings.step4: Click “Link account”: your browser opens Spotify's page, accept, then come back here.
settings.connectingHint: Finish signing in on the Spotify page opened in your browser (3 minutes at most).
settings.others: Other platforms: Tidal is being studied; Deezer no longer accepts new apps, Apple Music requires a paid developer membership, Beatport and Shazam offer no public access.
settings.previewHint: The ▶ button plays a 30-second preview in the application. The preview is requested from the service only when you click, then played straight from its servers: nothing is downloaded or kept.
settings.openHint: Site opened in your browser by each title's ↗ button (Charts, New releases, Wishlist). If the title already comes from that site, its page opens directly; otherwise it is an “artist title” search.

sites.source: Source page (Apple Music, Deezer or MusicBrainz)

preview.none: No preview found for this title, neither on Deezer nor on Apple Music.
preview.failed: The preview could not be played (connection or format).

labels.title: Labels
labels.hint: A list of major labels is offered in the New releases tab. Click ☆ to make a label a favorite: “All my favorites” searches the releases of all your favorites at once. Add missing labels below.

sets.intro: A set is an ordered list. For each transition: key compatibility (Camelot wheel) and BPM gap. Click a track to see suggestions that mix well after it. Drag the ⋮⋮ handle to reorder.
sets.createWith_one: The selected track will be added
sets.createWith_other: The {{count}} selected tracks will be added
sets.empty: Create a set on the left. Tip: select tracks in the library first, they will be added.
sets.emptySet: This set is empty. Select tracks in the library then “Add selection”, or drag them onto “Sets” in the sidebar.
sets.confirmDelete: Delete the set “{{name}}”? Tracks and files are not touched.
sets.xmlExported_one: {{count}} track exported to the XML file.
sets.xmlExported_other: {{count}} tracks exported to the XML file.
sets.noSuggestion: No compatible track found (a BPM and a key are needed).

compat.adjacent: Neighbour key (±1 on the Camelot wheel)

stats.noHistory: Import the Rekordbox history (Settings › DJ tools) to see the most played tracks.

tags.hint: Click a tag to add or remove it. Tags stay in the application (they are not written into files) and work as a filter and as a smart filter rule.
tags.none: No tag yet. Create one below (for example “Wedding”, “Cocktail”, “Dancefloor”, “Clean version”).
tags.confirmDelete: Delete the tag “{{name}}” ({{count}} tracks)? Tracks are not touched.

usb.title_one: Copy {{count}} track to a USB key
usb.title_other: Copy {{count}} tracks to a USB key
usb.hint: Files are copied (never moved), and every copy is verified. A file already there and identical is not copied again.

layouts.playlist: A folder named after the playlist

usb.name: Name (folder and playlist)
usb.m3u: Create an M3U8 playlist on the key
usb.offline_one: {{count}} track on an unplugged disk was not copied.
usb.offline_other: {{count}} tracks on an unplugged disk were not copied.

tools.title: DJ tools
tools.hint: Play history, backup, perceived loudness, analysis and repair. None of these tools changes the audio of your files.

plays.title: Play history
plays.hint: In Rekordbox, export the collection as XML (File › Export Collection in xml format): playlists in the “HISTORY” folder are read. You can also export a history playlist as M3U8 or TXT (right-click › Export). Each night counts once per track; re-importing does not double plays.
plays.imported: History imported: {{sessions}} night(s), {{plays}} new play(s), {{unmatched}} track(s) not found in the library.
plays.confirmClear: Clear the whole imported play history? Tracks and files are not touched.

backup.title: Library backup
backup.hint: Copies all your tracks to a backup disk, grouped by original disk. Only new or changed files are copied; every copy is verified; nothing is ever deleted in the backup (an older version is kept next to it, “(ancienne date)”).
backup.report: {{copied}} file(s) copied, {{skipped}} already up to date ({{size}} copied).
backup.done: Backup finished: {{copied}} copied, {{skipped}} already up to date.
backup.doneWithFailures_one: Backup finished, but {{count}} file could not be copied.
backup.doneWithFailures_other: Backup finished, but {{count}} files could not be copied.
backup.reminder: Your last backup is older than the chosen reminder.

loudness.title: Perceived loudness (LUFS)
loudness.hint: Measures the perceived loudness of each track (EBU R128 standard): “Loudness (LUFS)” column and “very loud” / “quiet” counters in Library health. Audio is never modified.
loudness.started: Loudness measurement started in the background.

analysis.title: BPM, key and energy analysis
analysis.hint: For tracks without BPM or key. Results are shown before being written; an existing value is never replaced (Rekordbox remains the reference). Reliability measured on your library: BPM right 33 times out of 34, key exact about 6 times out of 10 and mix-compatible 3 times out of 4. Energy (1 to 10) is an estimate.
analysis.run: Analyze tracks without BPM or key
analysis.startedSelection: Analysis of the selection started. Results will be reviewed in Settings › DJ tools.
analysis.startedHealth: Analysis started. Results will be reviewed in Settings › DJ tools.
analysis.reviewHint: Only missing values will be written (greyed values already exist and do not change). Locked fields are never touched. Ctrl+Z undoes.
analysis.nothing: No result to write. Run the analysis first.
analysis.applied_one: BPM and key written for {{count}} track.
analysis.applied_other: BPMs and keys written for {{count}} tracks.

dates.title: Broken dates
dates.settingsHint: Some files have a malformed date in their tags: for safety, the application then refuses to edit their tags. The repair only removes these unreadable dates (the file keeps the same size, audio and other tags do not move). Ctrl+Z restores the original bytes.
dates.hint: The unreadable dates below will be removed. Audio and other tags do not move. Ctrl+Z restores the exact original bytes.

remaster.pick: Select a track in the library, then come back here (or … › Remaster…).
remaster.abHint: “Before” plays the original at the same perceived loudness as the result: you compare quality, not volume. Settings are heard live.
remaster.stereoHint: Bass in mono: everything below the chosen frequency becomes identical on both channels (punchier and more stable on a club system). Width: 0% = mono, 100% = original, above = wider.
remaster.loudnessHint: Guide: −7 to −8 LUFS for club, −9 to −10 for a more dynamic sound, −14 for streaming. The limiter always keeps peaks under the ceiling.
remaster.spectrumHint: Click “Refresh” to compare the original and the result.
remaster.exported: “{{name}}” created: {{lufs}} LUFS, peak {{peak}} dB. Ctrl+Z moves it to quarantine.
remaster.batchStarted_one: Remaster of {{count}} track started in the background.
remaster.batchStarted_other: Remaster of {{count}} tracks started in the background.
remaster.batchRunning: A batch remaster is already running.
remaster.exportHint: The original is never modified: a new “… (Remaster).wav” file (24-bit) is created next to it, with tags and cover, the version extended with “Remaster”, and added to the library.
remaster.limits: What Remaster can do: loudness, low / high balance, density, stereo image. What it cannot do: bring back the highs lost in a low-quality MP3. Always compare before / after.
remaster.presetHint: A preset keeps every sound setting and the fades, but not the trim (start / end), which belongs to each track. An existing name is replaced.
remaster.zeroOff: 0 = off. Tip: click a number to type it, or use the ↑ ↓ arrows (Shift + arrow = step ×10).
remaster.trimHint: To a tenth of a second. Start 0 = from the beginning; end at maximum = to the end. Fade 0 = none. Trim and fades are heard while listening and applied to the exported file; the original is never touched.
remaster.pin: Keep visible at the top while adjusting
remaster.unpin: Stop keeping visible at the top
remaster.diffHint: Bars: what your settings add (above 0) or remove (below), frequency by frequency, at equal loudness.
remaster.matchedHint: both curves are set to the same perceived loudness: you compare balance, not volume.
remaster.realHint: real levels: the result looks louder if its volume was raised.
remaster.stereoViewHint: stereo width per frequency (0 dB = as much stereo as centre; very low = mono).
remaster.excerpt: Measured on the excerpt {{from}} → {{to}} (middle of the kept part), recomputed on every change.

rows.peakRowHint: Highest level reached (0 dB = digital maximum).
rows.dynamicsRowHint: Gap between peak and average level: the smaller, the more compressed.
rows.widthRowHint: Stereo energy relative to the centre, above 150 Hz (0 % = mono).
